_comment: doc 08 §2.13 / §3.3 — the notification table, owned SOLELY by doc 08 (report C-71). This file REPLACED the stand-in `data/ui.json.alerts.events` wholesale on 2026-08-19; ui.json now carries presentation only (row height, panel width, badge cap) and `in_app_alerts` (doc 12's foreground banner gate, C-72). Two consumers, one table: `ui/alerts_model.gd` reads `bindings` + `events` for the in-app feed, and `game/notifications/notification_router.gd` reads `classes` + `events` + `runtime` for the PUSH decision. They can never disagree about what class an event is, because there is only one answer written down.

delivery._comment: The ONE block in this file doc 13 owns (report C-71 draws the line at policy-vs-platform, and these are platform). No budget, no classes, no quiet hours — only how a decision that has already been made becomes an Android notification. `game/notifications/notification_scheduler.gd` and `native_notification_sink.gd` are the readers; doc 08's planner never looks at it.
delivery._comment_ids: Ids only have to be unique WITHIN a batch, because cancel_all() runs before every plan (doc 13 §2.5). 1000 up, one per accepted entry, reset on cancel — which is what makes the platform's persisted schedule trivially replaceable.
delivery._comment_doze: Alarms are inexact BY CHOICE: SCHEDULE_EXACT_ALARM/USE_EXACT_ALARM are Play-restricted to alarm-clock and calendar apps and requesting one risks the listing (doc 13 §2.6). Doze can therefore slip a fire by ~15 min, so anything with less lead than doze_slop_s + min_useful_lead_s would land after the thing it announces and is DROPPED rather than delivered late.
delivery._comment_resume: doc 08 §2.13: on resume every pending alarm is cancelled, because the catch-up has replaced the future they assumed. The tokens they spent come back with them unless they had already fired (notification_router.gd, replan_after_resume).
delivery._comment_channels: Channel display names come from data/strings.en.json under this prefix + the lowercased class id (ui_notif_channel_p1_critical). A channel's name is fixed at creation FOREVER — Android will not let an app rename one after the player has seen it — so these strings are effectively part of the install.
delivery._comment_offline: Which events can be predicted at pause time, by predictability class (report C-23). `deterministic` = the fire tick is already derivable from the save (construction, land development); `forecast` = pre-rolled by the Director and committed to the save (weather warnings). Everything else is emergent, which needs a projection, and projection ships DISABLED (runtime.emergent_projection_enabled).

classes._comment: doc 08 §3.3's four-class model, canonical. `capacity` / `window_minutes` / `min_gap_minutes` are the PUSH budget and are the most conservative numbers in the project by intent (C-72): doc 12's in-app rates in data/ui.json are ~3x these and are a different quantity. `in_app_class` is the one-way map onto doc 12's p1/p2/p3 keys, so a class has one name here and doc 12's gate still keys off its own. P4 exists in schema and ships silent (`mvp_enabled: false`) so it cannot be bolted on later without a migration.

events._comment: One row per notify_id. Copy is CONVENTIONAL, never authored here (doc 08 §3.3): `n_<key>_title` / `n_<key>_body` in data/strings.en.json, the same keys doc 13 renders for a push, so an in-app row and its push can never drift (G-8). Adding an event therefore touches this file and the string table and nothing else. `state` is doc 12's §2.3 state token — the glyph and colour the in-app row wears — and is the only presentation fact in this file, because it is a property of the EVENT (a broken main is critical wherever it is shown) rather than of the surface. `in_app: false` would push without a feed row; nothing uses it yet and it is here so the shape exists.
events._comment_wave17: doc 04 §4 authored `CapacityWarning` and `RollingBlackoutRotated` and neither ever reached a player; Wave 17's `grid_component_removed` is the third. `transformer_removed` does NOT aggregate — a transformer the player pulled out is a place and a decision, and the next one is a different place — while the rotation does, because a rolling blackout is one story however many times the pain moves. `capacity_warning` binds only band 2 (CRITICAL, r >= 0.95): WARNING is what the overlay is for, and a P3 that fired at 0.75 on every transformer in a growing city would be the notification the player turns off.
events._comment_water_gap: Doc 91 §18.2's exception, closed. Doc 05 emits a diagnostic half nobody read: a zone whose demand has outrun supply, a tank running down, a tank empty, a pump/treatment/source that FAILED (as opposed to `water_pump_tripped`, which is a recoverable lockout and was already wired), and the boil notice LIFTING — the pair `water_contamination_started` never had. All five describe a state the player can act on and none of them reached a screen. `water_capacity_shortage` is the one worth reading twice: doc 05 §2.9 says out loud that no repair job exists for it, so it is the only water alert whose answer is BUILD, and it was the quietest thing in the game.
events._comment_aggregate: doc 08 §3.3's `aggregate` decides the COOLDOWN KEY, and it is the difference between `major_fire` (false — a fire is a place, and the next fire is a different place) and `transformer_failed` (true — the grid is one story however many pieces of it fail). `incident_started` follows `major_fire`; `outage_major` follows `transformer_failed`, which is also the only reading consistent with its own copy, `{count} blocks are dark`.
events._comment_flood: Doc 07 §2.4's lower bands, which shipped invisible (defect A91-D-26). `road_flooded` above is the 350 mm IMPASSABLE band and was the only one a player ever heard about; these are the 100 mm and 200 mm bands under it, and `road_reopened` is the all-clear the closure never had. Two bands are deliberately absent and will stay absent. The 40 mm NUISANCE band is something to SEE, not something to be told: its consumer is game/render/flood_view.gd. And the recede is bound to `road_reopened` rather than to `flood_level_changed{band: dry}`, because `dry` fires whenever any cell drops back under 40 mm — after a shower that never closed anything — and `road_reopened` fires only for a cell that had actually been shut. The rule the whole flood family follows: NARRATE the bands that change what the player can do, DRAW the ones that only change how the street looks. Cooldowns are long because the field is per LAND BLOCK and a city-wide downpour crosses one band on twenty blocks inside a minute; `coalesce_by: notify_id` makes those one story and the cooldown keeps it one story for the rest of the storm.
events._comment_condition_bands: 99-PA PA-31 / doc 98 RR-149. Doc 02 §2.6's band table, as two notifications. WORN is the one that matters and it is the quietest thing here — P3, aggregated, half a game-day of cooldown — because 321 crossings of 0.85 over a 45-game-day curriculum arc is roughly seven a day and the answer to seven a day is ONE line that says how many and what it costs, not seven lines that each name a house. POOR is a rung up in severity and NOT in class: after doc 93 §Y1's ownership floor only buildings the CITY owns can get there at all, so a Poor row is always about an asset the player can actually repair. Neither is ever a P1: a worn city is a slow bill, not an emergency, and doc 08's critical channel is for the things that wake somebody up.
events._comment_auto_repair: 99-PA PA-33 / doc 98 RR-150. The receipt for a policy the player switched on: it spent their money while they were not looking, so it says how much. `aggregate` is false because the event ALREADY carries its own count — one pass, one line — and `@count` would overwrite a real number with 1. It cannot fire at the shipped default, which is manual.
events._comment_assistance: 99-PA PA-32 / doc 98 RR-148. ONE row for EIGHT sim events, and that is the whole design: `assistance_stepped` fires once per game-day for the seven days doc 03 §2.5a's founding grant tapers, and only the LAST one — `final: true`, the day the subsidy is gone and the city starts paying its own departments and fleet — is worth a notification. The other seven are doc 12 event-log rows and nothing else (data/ui.json.event_log.events), because a push a day for a week about a number that is going down on a published schedule is the notification budget spent on a thing the player cannot act on. P3 for the same reason: it is a fact to find, not an emergency.
events._comment_summary: The coalescing target (doc 08 §2.13.2). When three or more of one class would fire inside `coalesce_window_minutes` they collapse into ONE of these carrying the highest severity — one token, not three. It has no binding of its own: nothing in sim/ emits it, the router synthesises it.
events._comment_quiet_summary: What quiet hours defer to (doc 08 §2.13.3): ONE P3 at the end of the window, deliberately a rank below the coalescing summary — the things it carries were not urgent enough to bypass, so the thing that reports them at 08:00 must not arrive as though they were.
events._comment_p4: doc 08 §3.3's two P4 rows. The class ships disabled, so these emit nothing in MVP; they are here so the schema does not have to change when re-engagement lands.

bindings._comment: sim event → notify_id, in priority order: FIRST MATCH WINS, which is why this is an ARRAY and `events` above is an object. `match` is exact equality (JSON has one number type, so bools and numbers compare by value). `key` names the payload field that identifies the entity; `coalesce_by` picks `notify_id` (all dark blocks are one story) or `key` (each transformer is its own). `args` maps a copy placeholder onto a payload field or a derived value — `@count`, `@time`, `@id`, `@money:<field>`, `@number:<field>`. `class` on a binding OVERRIDES the event row's class, which is how one sim event whose payload carries its own urgency (an incident's `notification_priority`) reaches two different budgets without needing two sets of copy.

Water (doc 05). `water_main_break` and `water_freeze_break` are one emit site with a ternary on `frozen`, and they are two rows here because a main that split in the cold is a different repair and a different sentence.

Doc 05's diagnostic half (see `_comment_water_gap` above). The three `*_failed` types share ONE notify_id: a pump, a treatment plant and a source that have failed are the same sentence to a player and the same job to a crew, and three sets of copy would be three ways to say `send someone`. `water_tank_low` is deliberately log-only and has no row here — it is the warning BEFORE the thing worth waking someone for, and `water_tank_empty` is the thing.

Incidents (doc 06). `notification_priority` is the sim's own urgency and it is already the field data/audio.json picks the sting from; a P1 incident reaches doc 08's P1 budget through the class override rather than through a second notify_id, so the copy stays one sentence.

Doc 07 §2.4's bands, below the 350 mm one `road_closed_flood` already carried. `match` is exact equality on the band label FloodField puts in the payload, so the two rows are disjoint and their order between themselves does not matter; they sit after `road_closed_flood` because a tile that has just gone impassable is a road story before it is a weather one. `road_reopened` closes the pair the closure never had — it was emitted and consumed by tests only. A flood while the player is backgrounded is exactly what doc 08 §2.13's notifications exist for, and these are the rows that make one arrive.

Progression (doc 02). `city_level_changed` carries `from`/`to`, NOT `level` — the stand-in table read `level` and quietly rendered an empty title against the real event while passing its own fixture. Likewise `block_ready` carries `block`, not `block_id`. Both are fixed here against the emit sites in sim/population/progression_system.gd and sim/world/development_controller.gd.

runtime._comment: doc 08 §8's `notifications_runtime`. That block is filed under data/persistence.json in the doc; persistence.json does not exist in the repo yet, and splitting one policy across a file that is not there would mean the budget lived nowhere. It lives HERE, beside the classes it limits, and moves verbatim when persistence.json lands. Everything in it is doc 08's number, unchanged.
runtime._comment_quiet: doc 08 §2.13.3. Minutes past device-local midnight, so 1320 is 22:00 and 480 is 08:00 and the window WRAPS. Policy is `defer_to_end`: what quiet hours suppress collapses into one P3 summary when the window closes, rather than being lost. `allow_critical` is the player's explicit opt-in and ships OFF, so by default nothing wakes anybody — a P1 at 03:00 is in the ring and in the report at 08:00, informed rather than woken.
